The photo guide defines a structured data manifold where each photo contributes to an identity model through four primary dimensions: quantity, content clarity, variety, and quality. The quantity constraint ensures sufficient samples for statistical inference, while content clarity enforces minimal visual integrity for recognition. Variety introduces dimensionality to the feature space, enhancing robustness against adversarial perturbations. Quality ensures that the input signal is sufficiently informative for downstream processing. These primitives form a dual structure: one for probabilistic modeling (GSI) and one for action selection (GSE). Failure modes arise when any dimension violates its constraints—e.g., low quantity leads to underfitting, poor clarity causes misidentification, lack of variety results in brittle embeddings, and low quality degrades SNR. Each primitive maps to a distinct layer in the system architecture, enabling modular reasoning and error propagation analysis.
